text:
maya: kicked off the nightly perf suite — noticed a p95 spike on small-batch path, attaching quick dump
chris: did you re-run? could be noise from replay ordering
maya: re-ran 3x: two runs look fine, one shows p95=142ms vs baseline 98ms. kv_cache.hit_rate dropped 0.84 -> 0.62 in the noisy run
jordan: that smell like eviction storms. our replay harness shuffles request order unless we pass a seed. different order -> different cache contiguity -> hit-rate variance
priya: agreed. for apples-to-apples we should make replay deterministic by default and add a small "warmup prefixes" phase to populate KV cache before measurements
maya: also the CI alert triggers on a single-run p95 > threshold. that's causing noisy alerts for these stochastic cases
chris: suggestion: change alerting to require either 2-of-3 consecutive failures or compare against median of last 3 runs to reduce flakes
perf-bot: nightly-run failed: https://ci.redwood/internal/nightly/1799991234 — flamegraph & raw traces uploaded to artifact store
jordan: another angle: kernel selector sometimes falls back to float kernels for certain sequence-length distributions; that causes token latency jumps. we should emit kernel-selection decisions into per-request traces so we can correlate
priya: plan: (1) add --seed to replay harness, (2) add short KV warmup step, (3) make alert rule median-based or 2-of-3, (4) capture kernel-selection logs + flamegraphs to S3 for each nightly run
maya: example invocation i've been using locally:
```
./replay-harness \
  --profile=user_journey_A \
  --seed=42 \
  --shape=burst:20@200ms \
  --kv-warmup=5 \
  --out-traces=s3://redwood-perf/nightly/1799991234/
```
jordan: i'll open a PR for deterministic replay + kernel-selection logging. tagging @oncall for visibility
priya: also recommend we update the dashboard job to publish a small “stability” panel: median, interquartile p95, and hit-rate trend, plus a link to raw flamegraphs
maya: will update alert docs and dashboard job. if we do warmup + deterministic seed i expect much better night-to-night consistency :thumbsup:
chris: thanks — once PR is up i'll kick off a few runs and look at variance numbers
maya: sounds good. i'll paste links to runs here when available
